title: What moves the supply curve?

readouts.v: {cost==1 && tax==0 && n==3 ? "at the start" : (sq(own)<3*10*(own-1)-0.001 ? "shifted left" : (sq(own)>3*10*(own-1)+0.001 ? "shifted right" : "back at the start"))}

readouts.l: Quantity supplied at the own price

predict.q: The price of fertiliser and fuel rises. What happens to the strawberry farm's supply curve?

options.fb: Higher costs make each unit less profitable, so less is offered at every price: S shifts left (up).
Higher costs make each unit less profitable, so less is offered at every price: S shifts left, not right.

options.s: The point slides up along S
options.fb: The point slides only when the strawberries' own price changes. Costs shift the whole curve.

options.s: Nothing changes until the price of strawberries changes
options.fb: Supply depends on costs as well as price. A cost rise shifts S straight away.

task: Move the **input costs** control to "high" and watch S. Then try the **tax per unit** and **number of firms** sliders, and the **own price** slider to slide along S.

target.do: Set input costs to "high", then press Check.

takeaway: Only the good's own price moves producers **along** S; costs, taxes, subsidies, weather and the number of firms shift S.
explore: A tax shifts S up by the tax at every quantity; more firms shift S right; the own price only slides the point along S.
